arguments.title: FY2025 revenue in information memorandum does not match the audited accounts
arguments.text: The marketing document states FY2025 revenue of CHF 148.6 million [1], but the audited accounts show CHF 142.3 million [2], a gap of CHF 6.3 million (+4.4%). No reconciliation was found in the data room; valuation and leverage must be based on the audited figure.

citations.text: Revenue reached CHF 148.6 million in FY2025, up from CHF 131.0 million in FY2024, with adjusted EBITDA of CHF 26.8 million.

arguments.title: Brenntal Automotive GmbH can terminate on change of control
arguments.text: Brenntal Automotive GmbH can terminate its agreement if a third party acquires control without its consent [1]. It accounts for 31.2% of FY2025 revenue [2], so the acquisition itself puts that revenue at risk unless consent is obtained before signing. Legal due diligence has not reviewed this agreement [3].

citations.text: 14.2 If any third party acquires, directly or indirectly, more than 50% of the shares or voting rights in the Supplier without the Buyer's prior written consent, the Buyer may terminate this agreement with 90 days' written notice.
Brenntal Automotive GmbH, Share of revenue: 0.312
The Brenntal agreement was provided late and has not yet been reviewed.

arguments.title: FY2026 net leverage covenant headroom is thin
arguments.text: The model projects net leverage of 4.38x at the end of FY2026 [1] against a covenant maximum of 4.50x [2], a headroom of 2.7%. A revenue shortfall of CHF 4.0 million [3] at the plan EBITDA margin of 17.4% would lift leverage to 4.50x with net debt unchanged, at or above the covenant.

arguments.text: The information memorandum and the budget assume start of production in Q2 2026 [1], [2]. A later handwritten note records that it moved to Q1 2027 and that revenue will fall below budget [3]. The plan used for valuation and for the covenant test should be restated.
